entries.task_id: ambon malay|is|spoken in the indonesian province of maluku
entries.description: Ambon Malay is spoken in the Indonesian province of Maluku
entries.subject: Ambon Malay
entries.object: spoken in the Indonesian province of Maluku

spans.text: Ambon Malay is spoken in the Indonesian province of Maluku, located in the central and southern Moluccas Islands in eastern Indonesia, by about 200,000 native speakers (Gordon 2005) located on the island of Ambon, the neighbouring islands of Saparua, Haruku and Nusa Laut, along the southern coast of Seram Island and in urban locations in the southern Moluccas.

entries.task_id: where it|is|known as melajoe sini ‘malay here’)
entries.description: where it is known as Melajoe Sini ‘Malay here’)
entries.subject: where it

spans.text: There are also significant communities of speakers of Ambon Malay in Jakarta (the capital of Indonesia) and in the Netherlands (where it is known as Melajoe Sini ‘Malay here’).

entries.task_id: although it|is|regarded as a “low” variety when compared to indonesian
entries.description: Although it is regarded as a “Low” variety when compared to Indonesian
entries.subject: Although it
entries.object: regarded as a “Low” variety when compared to Indonesian

spans.text: Although it is regarded as a “Low” variety when compared to Indonesian, it is a “High” variety for speakers of vernacular languages in the Moluccas, and occupies a position between the vernaculars and Indonesian in terms of prestige.

entries.task_id: that malay|has|been spoken in ambon for over 1000 years
entries.description: that Malay has been spoken in Ambon for over 1000 years
entries.subject: that Malay
entries.object: been spoken in Ambon for over 1000 years

spans.text: Blust (1988) estimates that Malay has been spoken in Ambon for over 1000 years, though, without written records, it is difficult to know precisely how long Malay has been spoken in the region.
Ambon Malay has been influenced by the local vernacular languages of Ambon Island, some of which have been replaced by Ambon Malay.

entries.task_id: malay|was|known in trading centres throughout the region
entries.description: Malay was known in trading centres throughout the region
entries.subject: Malay
entries.object: known in trading centres throughout the region

spans.text: When Europeans first arrived in the Moluccas in the early 16th century, Malay was known in trading centres throughout the region, including Ambon, which, although it was not originally the source of the spices which traders sought, had a protected harbour in which traders traditionally waited out the monsoon season from February to May, a tradition which was adopted by European traders in the region as well.

entries.description: tradition which was adopted by European traders in the region as well
entries.subject: tradition which
entries.object: adopted by European traders in the region as well

spans.text: When Europeans first arrived in the Moluccas in the early 16th century, Malay was known in trading centres throughout the region, including Ambon, which, although it was not originally the source of the spices which traders sought, had a protected harbour in which traders traditionally waited out the monsoon season from February to May, a tradition which was adopted by European traders in the region as well.

entries.task_id: in ternate|fled|there in 1575
entries.description: in Ternate fled there in 1575
entries.subject: in Ternate

spans.text: Over time, this location gained importance for the Portuguese, especially after the Portuguese built a fort there in 1569 and after the Portuguese community which had settled in Ternate fled there in 1575.

entries.description:

entries.subject:
the

entries.object: their fort in Ambon to the Dutch

spans.text: During the era of extensive Portuguese trade in the area, which lasted until 1605, when the Portuguese surrendered their fort in Ambon to the Dutch, many Portuguese loan words entered the Malay spoken in the Moluccas.

entries.task_id: the malay|spoken|in the moluccas
entries.description: the Malay spoken in the Moluccas
entries.subject: the Malay

spans.text: During the era of extensive Portuguese trade in the area, which lasted until 1605, when the Portuguese surrendered their fort in Ambon to the Dutch, many Portuguese loan words entered the Malay spoken in the Moluccas.

entries.task_id: there|are|far more in ambon malay
entries.description: there are far more in Ambon Malay
entries.subject: there

spans.text: Although varieties of Malay in the western part of the Malay Archipelago have a significant number of loan words from Portuguese, there are far more in Ambon Malay, including kinship terms and pronouns (Abdurachman 1972).

entries.task_id: there|is|an even divide between christians and muslims
entries.description: there is an even divide between Christians and Muslims
entries.subject: there
entries.object: an even divide between Christians and Muslims

spans.text: On the island of Ambon today, there is an even divide between Christians and Muslims.

entries.task_id: has been|spoken|in ambon for many centuries
entries.description: has been spoken in Ambon for many centuries
entries.subject: has been

spans.text: Although Malay has been spoken in Ambon for many centuries, it is unclear precisely when the language began to change from a second language used as a lingua franca to a native language used by a specific community.

entries.task_id: there|was|indeed a community of native malay speakers
entries.description: there was indeed a community of native Malay speakers
entries.subject: there
entries.object: indeed a community of native Malay speakers

spans.text: It is certain that by the early 19th century, there was indeed a community of native Malay speakers, and today the Ambon Malay language continues to gain new speakers at the expense of speakers of vernacular languages throughout the central and southern Moluccas.

entries.description: are still spoken on Ambon (chiefly on the northern Hitu peninsula of the island
entries.subject: are still
entries.object: on Ambon (chiefly on the northern Hitu peninsula of the island

spans.text: The vernaculars which are still spoken on Ambon (chiefly on the northern Hitu peninsula of the island, by Muslim communities) and the Lease Islands (Haruku, Saparua, Nusa Laut) are Asilulu, Hitu, Haruku, Laha, Larike-Wakasihu, Nusa Laut, Saparua, Seit-Kaitetu, and Tulehu.

entries.description: was once spoken on Ambon
entries.subject: was once

spans.text: A Portuguese creole, now extinct, was once spoken on Ambon.

entries.description: Ambon Malay are at least bilingual
entries.subject: Ambon Malay

spans.text: All speakers of Ambon Malay are at least bilingual, with many speaking more than two language varieties.

entries.description: all speakers are able to use the national language
entries.subject: all speakers
entries.object: able to use the national language

spans.text: Nearly all speakers are able to use the national language, Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia) with varying degrees of competence.

entries.task_id: indonesian|is|used in education
entries.description: Indonesian is used in education
entries.subject: Indonesian

spans.text: Indonesian is used in education, government administration, the media and some workplaces, with Ambon Malay serving as the language of home and community and daily interaction.

entries.description: Ambon Malay is rarely found in the media
entries.subject: Ambon Malay

spans.text: Ambon Malay is rarely found in the media, apart from some newspaper headlines, newspaper cartoons and columns, advertising and special features on radio and television.

entries.task_id: there|is|variation in ambon malay
entries.description: There is variation in Ambon Malay
entries.subject: There

spans.text: There is variation in Ambon Malay, with distinct dialects developing, chiefly in urban centres, in other regions of the province.

entries.task_id: ambon malay|remain|undescribed
entries.description: Ambon Malay remain undescribed
entries.subject: Ambon Malay

spans.text: These variants of Ambon Malay remain undescribed.

entries.task_id: ambon malay|has|five vowels
entries.description: Ambon Malay has five vowels
entries.subject: Ambon Malay

spans.text: In common with other contact Malay varieties of eastern Indonesia, Ambon Malay has five vowels.

entries.task_id: it|is|likely that the trade language which lexified ambon malay
entries.description: It is likely that the trade language which lexified Ambon Malay
entries.subject: It
entries.object: likely that the trade language which lexified Ambon Malay

spans.text: It is likely that the trade language which lexified Ambon Malay, Vehicular Malay, had a schwa, which was lost when the parent variety of eastern Indonesian contact Malay varieties, Eastern Indonesia Trade Malay, was formed.
